You are an eighth-grade student taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in your grade. Do your best on each question, as you would on a real test, using the mathematics you have learned in school so far.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
[Image: A pentagon. Going from the bottom left corner and working clockwise, the corners are labeled as A, E, D, C, and B. There is a line drawn from A to D, and also from A to C.]

What is the sum of all the interior angles of pentagon ABCDE?
Show your work.

Answer: ____

Figure, described in words:
A pentagon ABCDE with vertices labeled clockwise starting from the bottom left: A at the bottom left, E at the middle left, D at the top apex, C at the middle right, and B at the bottom right. Two internal line segments are drawn from vertex A: one segment connects A to D, and another connects A to C, dividing the interior of the pentagon into three triangles: triangle AED, triangle ADC, and triangle ABC.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: The pentagon can be divided into 3 triangles by the diagonals AD and AC: triangle AED, triangle ADC, and triangle ABC. Each triangle has interior angles summing to 180 degrees, so the pentagon's interior angles sum to 3 × 180° = 540°. Check using the formula (n − 2) × 180° with n = 5: (5 − 2) × 180° = 3 × 180° = 540°. Answer: 540 degrees.
